sizeNote: Sizes are rounded and only a gentle guide: head to bottom up to week 19, head to heel from week 20. Every baby grows in their own way.

1: Any bleeding, or bleeding with tummy pain
Bad tummy pain that doesn’t ease
Being sick so often you can’t keep fluids down
Pain or burning when you pee
2: Tummy pain or cramps that don’t ease
A bad headache, blurry vision or sudden swelling
From about 24 weeks: movements slowing down, stopping or changing (call straight away)
3: Movements slowing down, stopping or changing: call straight away, day or night
Any bleeding, or your waters breaking
A bad headache, blurry vision or sudden swelling of the face, hands or feet

kicks: There’s no set number of kicks to reach. Get to know your baby’s own pattern. If movements slow down, stop or change, call your maternity unit straight away, day or night. Don’t wait until the next day.

For baby: Car seat for the ride home

weeks.baby: A tiny ball of cells is settling into the lining of the womb.
weeks.you: A missed period may be the first sign. Start folic acid if you haven’t yet.
weeks.tip: Take over cooking for a while; smells can feel strong.

weeks.baby: The brain, spine and heart are starting to form.
weeks.you: You may notice tiredness and tender breasts.
weeks.tip: Ask how they’re feeling, and really listen.

weeks.baby: A tiny heart has started to beat.
weeks.you: Morning sickness can start now, at any time of day. Small snacks often help.
weeks.tip: Keep crackers and water by the bed.
weeks.chk: Your first check-up: a scan may show the heartbeat.

weeks.baby: Little buds are growing that will become arms and legs.
weeks.you: Needing to pee more often is normal now.
weeks.tip: Join the first appointment if you can.

weeks.baby: Fingers and toes are beginning to form.
weeks.you: Big feelings are okay. Your body is doing a lot.
weeks.tip: Read up together on what’s coming.

weeks.baby: All the main organs have started to form.
weeks.you: Nausea may be strongest around now. Ginger and rest can help.
weeks.tip: Plan easy dinners for tired evenings.

weeks.baby: Tiny nails are starting to grow.
weeks.you: Your clothes may start to feel a little snug.
weeks.tip: Start a small savings plan for baby things.

weeks.baby: Bones are starting to harden.
weeks.you: You may start to feel a little more energy soon.
weeks.tip: Go for gentle walks together.

weeks.baby: Fingers can curl and the mouth can make sucking movements.
weeks.you: The end of the first trimester is close.
weeks.tip: Decide together when and how to share the news.
weeks.chk: First-trimester screening (11–13 weeks): a scan and an optional blood test.

weeks.baby: Fingerprints are forming on those tiny fingertips.
weeks.you: Nausea often eases from now. You may feel more like yourself.
weeks.tip: Plan something fun while energy is back.

weeks.baby: Your baby can squint, frown and make faces.
weeks.you: More blood flow can give your skin a glow.
weeks.tip: Start a bump photo series together.

weeks.baby: Your baby can sense light through closed eyelids.
weeks.you: A blocked nose or bleeding gums can happen. Brush gently.
weeks.tip: Start a list of names, just for fun.

weeks.baby: Muscles are getting stronger and the head is held more upright.
weeks.you: You may feel the first flutters any time from now.
weeks.tip: Help with anything heavy.
weeks.chk: Ask about the whooping cough (Tdap) vaccine, recommended between 16 and 32 weeks.

weeks.baby: A layer of fat is starting to form under the skin.
weeks.you: A pillow between your knees can make side-sleeping comfier.
weeks.tip: Offer a foot rub.

weeks.baby: The ears are in place, and your baby may start to hear.
weeks.you: Feeling dizzy? Stand up slowly.
weeks.tip: Book antenatal classes together.

weeks.baby: A creamy coating (vernix) now protects the skin.
weeks.you: Your tummy stretching can cause aches low down.
weeks.tip: Plan to go to the detailed scan together.

weeks.baby: Your baby can hear muffled sounds now. Talking and singing to the bump counts.
weeks.you: You may feel flutters, a bit like bubbles.
weeks.tip: Evenings can be lively. Put a hand on the bump together after dinner.
weeks.chk: The detailed scan (around 18–22 weeks) looks closely at how your baby is growing.

weeks.baby: Your baby swallows a little fluid and may taste some of what you eat.
weeks.you: Heartburn? Smaller meals and sitting up after eating can help.
weeks.tip: Talk and sing to the bump; your baby can hear you.

weeks.baby: Eyebrows and eyelashes are growing.
weeks.you: Itchy, stretching skin? A plain moisturiser can soothe it.
weeks.tip: Look at prams and car seats together.

weeks.baby: Your baby may move in response to loud sounds.
weeks.you: Swollen ankles? Put your feet up when you can.
weeks.tip: Find out about parental leave together.

weeks.baby: The lungs are growing tiny branches.
weeks.you: Get to know your baby’s pattern of movements.
weeks.tip: Feel for kicks together.

weeks.baby: Hands can open and close, and your voice is becoming familiar.
weeks.you: Trouble sleeping? Try your side, with pillows for support.
weeks.tip: Plan a quiet weekend away or at home.

weeks.baby: The eyes are getting ready to open.
weeks.you: Leg cramps at night? Stretch your calves before bed.
weeks.tip: Get the baby’s sleeping space ready.
weeks.chk: Glucose test (24–28 weeks) checks for diabetes in pregnancy.

weeks.baby: Your baby sleeps and wakes in regular cycles.
weeks.you: The third trimester starts next week. A good time to think about classes.
weeks.tip: Learn the signs of labour together.

weeks.baby: Your baby can blink and open the eyes.
weeks.you: From now, going to sleep on your side is safest for your baby.
weeks.tip: Extra pillows help with side-sleeping.
weeks.chk: Check-ups often become every 2 weeks from now.

weeks.baby: Kicks and stretches are getting stronger.
weeks.you: Feeling breathless? Your bump is pushing up. Rest when you need to.
weeks.tip: Take over the shopping runs.

weeks.baby: The brain is growing quickly.
weeks.you: Practice tightenings (Braxton Hicks) may come and go.
weeks.tip: Fit the car seat and practise with it.

weeks.baby: Your baby can turn the head from side to side.
weeks.you: A little leak when you sneeze can happen. Pelvic floor exercises help.
weeks.tip: Learn how to change a nappy.

weeks.baby: Your baby practises breathing movements.
weeks.you: A good week to start packing your hospital bag.
weeks.tip: Plan the route to the hospital.

weeks.baby: Bones are hardening, but the skull stays soft for birth.
weeks.you: Tiredness may come back. Short rests help.
weeks.tip: Pack your own bag too: snacks, charger, a change of clothes.

weeks.baby: Fingernails now reach the fingertips.
weeks.you: Think about who will be with you at the birth.
weeks.tip: Keep your phone charged and switched on.

weeks.baby: There’s less room, so you may feel more rolls and stretches. Movements carry on right up to birth.
weeks.you: Your baby may drop lower, which can make breathing easier.
weeks.tip: Cook and freeze a few meals for after the birth.

weeks.baby: Your baby may be settling head-down.
weeks.you: Your bag is ready by the door. Rest when you can.
weeks.tip: Wash the baby clothes.
weeks.chk: Check-ups often become weekly from now.

weeks.baby: The lungs keep getting ready for the first breath.
weeks.you: Signs of labour: regular tightenings, waters breaking, or a show.
weeks.tip: Know who to call, and when.

weeks.baby: Your baby can grip tightly with those little hands.
weeks.you: Rest, eat well and keep your bag handy.
weeks.tip: Keep things calm and rest together.

weeks.baby: The brain is still growing fast.
weeks.you: Waiting can feel long. Gentle walks may help you feel good.
weeks.tip: Be ready to time contractions.

weeks.baby: Babies arrive when they’re ready.
weeks.you: Keep noticing your baby’s movements and call if anything feels different.
weeks.tip: Patience and kindness go a long way.
weeks.chk: Past your due date? Your doctor will talk you through the next steps.
